Predicates:
FinancialAid(x) ::: x is provided with financial aid.
Applicant(x) ::: x is applying to take the GRE.
Hardship(x) ::: x proves economic hardship.
SingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
FewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available.
LiveInSingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
ResourcesAvailable(x) ::: x has resources available.
ApplyingGRE(x) ::: x is applying to take the GRE.
CostGRE(c, y) ::: cost of GRE test is y for c.
Cheaper(y, z) ::: y is cheaper than z.
Cost(c, y) ::: cost of c is y.
ProvidedFinancialAid(x) ::: x is provided with financial aid.
LiveInSingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
FewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available.
ApplyingGRE(x) ::: x is applying to take the GRE.
CostGRE(c, y) ::: cost of the GRE test is y.
Cost(c, y) ::: cost of c is y.
Cheaper(y, z) ::: y is cheaper than z.
Premises:
CostGRE(GRE, 205) ∧ Cost(GRE, 205) ∧ Cheaper(205, 300) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE, which is cheaper than $300.
∀x (Applicant(x) → (Hardship(x) ∨ LiveInSingleParentFamily(x) ∨ FewResources(x))) ::: Those applying can prove hardship or have few resources or live in a single-parent family.
LiveInSingleParentFamily(Tom) ∧ FewResources(Tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family and has few resources.
ApplyingGRE(Tom) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE.
Conclusion:
¬∃x (FinancialAid(x) ∧ ApplyingGRE(x)) ::: No one taking the GRE has financial aid provided to them by something.
